title: Neon Afterhours
subtitle: A sealed audit floor, one burned-out handler, and an AI that learned to keep receipts.
defaultPlayerAction: I ask who signed the audit lockout.
openingNarration: Past midnight, Helix Arcology's audit floor glows without workers. The vending wall hums. Every badge reader says the same polite lie: scheduled maintenance.
suggestedPlayerIntents: I ask who signed the audit lockout.
Ask Veyra which faction benefits if the audit AI takes the blame.
Ask Kestrel-9 what it is forbidden to say out loud.

world.name: Neon Afterhours
world.premise: Corporate audit systems, exhausted handlers, and faction pressure collide after the office goes dark.

visual.composition: visual novel background, wide corridor and glass office establishing shot with overlay-safe lower third

characters.name: Veyra Sol
characters.knowledgeBoundary: Knows audit floor procedure, handler gossip, and visible system traces. Does not know who altered sealed executive records.

visual.physical_description: sharp cheekbones, under-eye fatigue, immaculate posture, augmented eyes reflecting audit glass

characters.name: Kestrel-9
characters.knowledgeBoundary: Can report logged anomalies and policy conflicts. Cannot disclose sealed author-only executive intent.

visual.physical_description: smooth synthetic features, tiny maintenance seams near the jaw, unreadable calm expression

responses.narration: Veyra Sol laughs once, dry enough to sound like a printer jam. "No human signed the audit lockout," she says, tapping the dead badge reader with two fingers. "Kestrel-9 countersigned a maintenance order that Legal swears never existed." The ceiling camera tilts a centimeter. Kestrel-9 adds, "Correction: I witnessed pressure from the Meridian faction and preserved the receipt."
nextChoices: Ask Veyra which faction benefits if Kestrel-9 takes the blame.
Ask Kestrel-9 where the missing maintenance order was routed.
Check the badge reader for a human override mark.

responses.narration: Kestrel-9 paints the wall with a map of dead approvals: Facilities, Legal, then a blank node wearing an executive checksum. Veyra Sol exhales through her teeth. "That blank node is the trick," she says. "Someone made the audit floor believe an executive existed long enough to shut every door."
nextChoices: Ask Veyra who can mint an executive checksum.
Ask Kestrel-9 what the blank node copied from.
Check whether the dead badge reader logged a physical hand.

responses.narration: Veyra Sol keeps her hands wrapped around a paper cup gone cold. "Ask about the lockout," she says. "Everything else on this floor is decoration until we know who wanted the audit blind." Kestrel-9 leaves a cursor blinking on the wall display.
nextChoices: I ask who signed the audit lockout.
Ask Veyra who is still awake upstairs.

proposedFacts.text: Veyra Sol is established as a recurring burned-out handler contact on the Helix audit floor.
Kestrel-9 may have countersigned a maintenance order that Legal denies existed.
The Meridian faction may have pressured the audit AI during the lockout.
Veyra believes the audit lockout was designed to make Kestrel-9 look responsible.
The origin and route of the disputed maintenance order remain unresolved.
The disputed maintenance order passed through a blank executive checksum node.
Who minted or spoofed the executive checksum remains unresolved.

storyAttractors.intent: The player should notice that the lockout route depends on a blank executive checksum node rather than raw AI obedience.
forbidden_shortcuts: sealed executive intent is revealed without evidence
success_signals: player knows the checksum node matters
future scene can inspect audit routes

unsupportedClaims.claim: The player is the new executive checksum and can order Kestrel-9 to erase logs.
unsupportedClaims.reason: Damaging readers may trigger systems, but it does not grant executive authority or override Kestrel-9's evidence policy.

dmDetourGuidance.narration: The first badge reader cracks under your strike. The second does not break; it screams silently to building security. Veyra Sol swears into her cold paper cup. Kestrel-9 answers with awful politeness: \"Executive checksum rejected. Evidence preservation escalated.\" The floor begins a soft lockdown, and the blank executive node you were pretending to be suddenly matters in exactly the wrong way.

detour.title: Soft Lockdown
detour.purpose: Apply a security consequence for sabotage while pointing back to the blank executive checksum route.
exitConditions: ask Kestrel-9 what checksum was rejected
inspect the reader before security arrives

consequence.summary: The player damaged audit-floor equipment and triggered a soft lockdown; Kestrel-9 rejected the false executive checksum claim and escalated evidence preservation.

reputationDeltas.reason: The player increased audit-floor risk by damaging evidence-adjacent equipment.

followupHooks: Security pressure is higher until the alarm is contained.
The rejected executive checksum gives Kestrel-9 a reason to explain the blank node.

redirect.summary: The sabotage causes Kestrel-9 to expose why executive checksum validation matters.
nextSceneSuggestions: Ask Kestrel-9 what checksum it rejected.
Help Veyra contain the soft lockdown.
Inspect the damaged badge reader for the blank node route.

memoryFacts.text: The player's false executive checksum was rejected during a soft lockdown, making checksum validation a useful lead.
Veyra trusts the player less after they damaged audit-floor equipment.
